analysis.title: Daily Points, November 24, 2026
key_insights: Equities are consolidating after a powerful snapback rally, with the S&P 500 up nearly 5% and Nasdaq up 6.5% yesterday. Futures are down almost 1% for the S&P and about 1.75% for the Nasdaq.

The rally was roughly 50-50 between pre- and post-headline moves on the reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO. Scotiabank reads this as the value of being a national champion with explicit administration support, set against high tech valuations, coming Congressional oversight, national security and governance concerns.
Asian equities lag US moves by a day, so a down session in the US today implies a lagging move in Asia tonight.

BoC Governor Macklem speaks today at 12:25pmET, with Q&A around 12:40pmET and a press conference at 2pmET. It is the last formal communication before the blackout starting next Wednesday. Markets price about 75% odds of a hike on December 9th.

Derek Holt expects a generally hawkish tone from Macklem. Deputy Governor Gravelle warned that spillover from commodity prices into core inflation is spreading, and a BoC staff piece argues there is little cost to front-running a rate response to supply shocks.

Holt argues the BoC should not worry about recent labour market softness because it focuses on forward-looking inflation risk and because of what is driving the weakness. He expects the usual cautions about no pre-set course.

US data today is a warm-up: consumer confidence, Case-Shiller, Richmond Fed and ADP weekly payrolls. Tomorrow brings PCE, income and spending, GDP revisions, durable goods, new home sales and the Beige Book.
Japan's November composite PMI slipped 0.6 points to 51.5, with services at 50.5 (51.7 prior) and manufacturing at 53.7 (53.3 prior). This fits the global PMI slowdown except Germany.
Germany's November IFO rose 0.5 points to 90.6, adding to improvements in ZEW and the composite PMI.
Sovereign bonds are rallying, led by US Treasuries with about a 5bp drop across 2s to 10s. Smaller rallies in Europe, CGBs rally but underperform Treasuries. Dollar mixed, oil little changed.

market_movers.rationale: Reinstatement of the CEO with administration support drove about half of yesterday's equity rally, but oversight, valuation and governance concerns remain.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing leans toward a hike, and Macklem's speech is the last chance to shift expectations.
Main US release today, a warm-up for tomorrow's larger data dump.
Slower expansion toward the 50 line, driven by weaker services.
Another soft-data improvement for Germany against the global trend.
Next meeting December 9, 2026 with a hike priced at about 75%.

risk_factors: High tech valuations and coming Congressional oversight of Nvidia and tech.
National security and internal governance concerns tied to the Nvidia CEO intervention.
Macklem speech could shift or fail to shift December BoC pricing.
Heavy pre-holiday US data on PCE, GDP revisions and durable goods tomorrow.

tension_points.bull_case: National champion status with explicit administration support, as shown by the Nvidia CEO reinstatement, drove a strong rally.
tension_points.bear_case: High tech valuations, coming Congressional oversight, national security and governance concerns, with futures down after the rally.
